---

## Story Goal

On `web/src/pages/customers/CustomerScreenPage.tsx`, add a **Sign-in** section that lets an agent grant an account to a customer who does not already have one.

User-visible outcomes:

1. If `customer.userId` is `null`, the section shows a **"Grant sign-in"** button. On click it POSTs to the CRM-65 endpoint, disables while in flight, and on success replaces itself with a **single, plain, unmasked** rendering of the returned initial password plus the account email. The password disappears on any navigation or reload of the screen and is never re-fetchable.
2. If `customer.userId` is not `null`, the section renders a short statement (e.g. "This customer already has a sign-in.") — **no button**, because an action that will be refused is worse than no action.
3. Field-scoped refusals from the API mark the offending field and render the shared error copy from `t.errors[code]`.
4. The submit button cannot be double-pressed while a request is in flight.
5. Every string comes from both `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts` (BR-6).

**Explicitly out of scope:** any change under `api/`; any portal / self-service screen; persisting or re-showing the initial password after the agent leaves the screen.

## Frontend Tasks

### 1 — Extend the customer type with `userId`

**File:** `web/src/pages/customers/useCustomer.ts`

Add `userId: string | null` to `type Customer` (currently **lines 7–14**). No other change to this hook. The value is served by the CRM-63/CRM-65 endpoint; if the field is absent the branch treats it as `null`.

### 2 — New hook: `useGrantSignIn`

**Create file:** `web/src/pages/customers/useGrantSignIn.ts`

Mirror `useWriteNote.ts` (**lines 1–28**) exactly:

```ts
import { useCallback } from 'react';

import { request } from '../../shared/api/client';
import { useRequest } from '../../shared/hooks';

export type GrantSignInResult = {
  userId: string;
  email: string;
  initialPassword: string;
};

export function useGrantSignIn(customerId: string) {
  const { status, error, run } = useRequest<GrantSignInResult>();

  const grant = useCallback(
    () =>
      run(() =>
        request<GrantSignInResult>(`/customers/${customerId}/sign-in`, {
          method: 'POST',
        }),
      ),
    [run, customerId],
  );

  return { status, error, grant, result: undefined as GrantSignInResult | undefined };
}
```

Return `data` from `useRequest` (rename `data` → `result` in the destructure) so the caller can render the plaintext password from the same object the POST returned — **not** from any cache or state that could be re-read after navigation. Confirm the field name (`initialPassword`) against the CRM-65 response before merging.

### 3 — Render the sign-in section on the customer screen

**File:** `web/src/pages/customers/CustomerScreenPage.tsx`

1. Import `useGrantSignIn` next to `useWriteNote` (near **line 22**).
2. Instantiate it below `const note = useWriteNote(id);` (**line 35**): `const signIn = useGrantSignIn(id);`.
3. Between the **contacts** `Card` (ends **line 97**) and the **openTickets** `Heading` (**line 99**), insert a new `Card` titled `t.customerScreen.signInTitle`. Inside:
   - If `customer.userId !== null`: render `<Text variant="muted">{t.customerScreen.signInAlready}</Text>`. **No button.**
   - Else if `signIn.status === 'success' && signIn.result`: render the plaintext credentials inside an `<Isolated>` block (email is LTR — see the `Isolated` usage at **lines 91, 94**):
     ```tsx
     <Stack gap={1}>
       <Text>{t.customerScreen.signInCreated}</Text>
       <Text><Isolated>{signIn.result.email}</Isolated></Text>
       <Text><Isolated>{signIn.result.initialPassword}</Isolated></Text>
       <Text variant="muted">{t.customerScreen.signInReadItOut}</Text>
     </Stack>
     ```
     Do **not** copy the password into component state, `localStorage`, or the URL. Do not render a "copy to clipboard" affordance — the agent reads it over the phone, once, then the screen changes and it is gone.
   - Else: render the button:
     ```tsx
     <Button
       disabled={signIn.status === 'loading'}
       onClick={() => void signIn.grant().catch(() => {})}
     >
       {signIn.status === 'loading' ? t.customerScreen.signInGranting : t.customerScreen.signInGrant}
     </Button>
     ```
     The `disabled` guard prevents the double-press acceptance criterion (same pattern as the notes button at **line 152**).
4. Below the button, mirror the notes error branch (**lines 155–160**): when `signIn.status === 'error' && signIn.error`, render `<ErrorState title={t.customerScreen.signInFailed} body={t.errors[signIn.error.code as keyof typeof t.errors] ?? t.errors.INTERNAL} />`. If the API returns a field-scoped refusal (e.g. code + `field`), surface `t.customerScreen.signInFieldError` next to that field.
5. Do **not** call `reload()` after a successful grant — that would fire a second `/customers/${id}` request and break the single-request assertion the screen test enforces. The success view is rendered straight from `signIn.result`.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Customer already has a sign-in (`customer.userId !== null`).** Trigger: initial render. Expected: statement only, no button. Enforced in the branch inserted in `CustomerScreenPage.tsx` between the contacts `Card` and open-tickets `Heading`.
- **Double-click during POST.** Trigger: agent clicks twice quickly. Expected: only one request; button disabled while `signIn.status === 'loading'` (same pattern as note submit at `CustomerScreenPage.tsx:152`).
- **API returns 409 "already has a sign-in" (race with another agent).** Trigger: two agents open the screen at once. Expected: error copy from `t.errors[code]` is rendered by the `ErrorState`; **no** plaintext password is shown. The `signIn.status === 'success'` branch requires `signIn.result` truthy, so a rejected promise cannot fall through to the credentials view.
- **API returns a validation refusal naming a field.** Expected: the field is marked (aria-invalid + inline copy) and the shared `t.errors[code]` sentence is shown — no ad-hoc strings.
- **Navigation after success.** Trigger: agent clicks another link, or reloads. Expected: `signIn.result` lives only in the component; unmount discards it. Do not persist to localStorage/URL/cache.
- **Screen reload via retry button (`ErrorState` `onRetry={reload}`).** After `reload()`, `useCustomer` re-runs and `screen` changes; the `signIn` hook's local state is unaffected but the password view is inside the same subtree — a successful grant, then a reload, must still not re-display the old password. `useEffect(() => setAdded([]), [screen])` at **line 47** is the precedent for clearing local state when `screen` changes; add a similar effect for `signIn` if the executor confirms the plaintext survives across `reload()` calls.
- **RTL rendering of email / password.** Both are LTR runs; wrap in `<Isolated>` as at `CustomerScreenPage.tsx:91, 94`. A password containing digits and punctuation would otherwise reorder in Arabic paragraphs.
- **Hardcoded-string test on new separators or punctuation.** Any `·`, `—`, `:` typed between tags will fail `no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` — use a module constant (see `SEPARATOR` at **line 28**) or move the punctuation into the resource string.

## Review note

Three corrections, and one of them was the plan reading a field that does not
exist.

1. **`customer.userId` is not what the API answers with.** The plan branched on
   it in three places. `CUSTOMERS-6-API` returns `hasSignIn`, a boolean, and
   deliberately not the user's id: a screen needs to know that a grant has
   happened so it can say so instead of offering an action that will be
   refused, and whose account it is belongs to identity. The plan guessed a
   field name from the column name.

2. **Two Jira keys were wrong** — `CUSTOMERS-4-API` cited as CRM-63, which is
   CUSTOMERS-4-WEB. `verify-plan` caught both. This intake was written before
   `scripts/story-keys.txt` existed, so its standing hints still told the
   planner to take keys from `backlog.txt`, which has none. The hint has been
   refreshed in all sixty-one intakes; the four plans still to be generated
   will have somewhere to read it (L-54).

3. **The password's disappearance is not implemented, it is inherited.** The
   plan asked that it "disappear on any navigation or reload and never be
   re-fetchable". Nothing had to be written for that: the hook holds it in
   `useRequest`'s state, no route reads it back, and the component unmounts on
   navigation. A test pins the reload behaviour, and it was watched in a
   browser as well — after a reload the card is gone and the statement stands
   in its place.

Looked at, not only tested: the section renders in the right place on the real
screen, the password comes back in full, and the sentence sits above it rather
than below. Worth saying plainly — the warning is body text at the same weight
as everything around it. On the one screen in this product that shows a secret
once, that is arguably too quiet, and it is a style decision no story owns.
